memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"The priest shall burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons. You are to give the right thigh of your fellowship offerings to the priest as a contribution."'" - Lev 7:31-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The breast and the right thigh — the two best cuts of meat on the animal — go to the priests.

God gave His servants the choice portions. Not the scraps that nobody wanted. Not what was left after the family had eaten. The best.

That is worth reflecting on in how we treat those who serve God's people. Churches sometimes expect their pastors, missionaries, and workers to live on the leftovers — underpaid, over-expected, quietly assumed to be fine because ministry is supposed to be sacrificial. God's own arrangement was more generous than that.

Paul told Timothy, The elders who direct the affairs of the church well are worthy of double honour, especially those whose work is preaching and teaching (1 Tim 5:17). And he added the reason: The worker deserves his wages.

But this cuts toward those who serve as well. The priest received the best cut precisely so that his heart would remain grateful rather than grasping. The moment he began to feel entitled to it, something had gone wrong — as it did badly with Eli's sons, who demanded the choice portions by force (1 Sam 2:15-16).

Generosity from one side, gratitude from the other. That is how God designed it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do those who serve me spiritually receive my best or my leftovers?
2. If I serve others, do I receive what comes with gratitude or with entitlement?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, make me generous toward those who serve You, and grateful for whatever You provide through Your people. Amen.
